sections.h2: Who bills property tax in Cape Coral?
sections.html:
Cape Coral sits in Lee County, so the Lee County Tax Collector mails and collects your bill, while the Lee County Property Appraiser sets the value and handles exemptions. The city only sets its own millage rate and its special assessments.

That split explains most phone calls. Questions about your value, mailing address or exemptions go to the appraiser's office at 239-533-6100. Questions about paying, receipts and refunds go to the tax collector. Questions about a specific levy on the bill go to the authority named on the bill.

QuickFacts puts Cape Coral at 236,264 people in its July 2025 estimate, a 21.8% jump over the 2020 base. Land area is 106.02 square miles, and owners occupy 77.2% of homes. Typical home value in the 2020 to 2024 survey is $373,500, and a quarter of the population has passed 65. Cape Coral's Census table also records 14,390 veterans and a 92.8% high school graduation rate among adults.

The table also shows 82,914 households averaging 2.59 people, rent of $1,858 at the median and a 29.9 minute average trip to work. Most residents stay put: 88.2% were in their home a year before the survey.

sections.h2: What does the City of Cape Coral charge on top of the county?
sections.html:
The city levies an operating millage rate, and its own news release says council kept that rate at 5.1471 mills in the Fiscal Year 2027 budget approved at the September 24 hearing. Each mill raises one dollar on every thousand dollars of taxable value, and the city rate is a single line among several authorities on your bill.

The same release says the budget keeps the Fire Service Assessment at 81 percent. Special assessments such as fire and solid waste appear on the tax bill as non-ad valorem charges, which are flat amounts that do not depend on your home's value.

The release also lists where the money goes: $99.2 million for the Police Department, $91.7 million for Fire, $12.9 million for road repaving and $50.4 million for the municipal charter school system. A seller can use those line items to explain to a buyer what the city levy supports.

  • Ad valorem lines: city, county, school board and special districts, each with its own millage.
  • Non-ad valorem lines: city fire and solid waste assessments and similar service charges.
  • Your parcel's exact figures: the city's Property Checkbook tool lists the city tax, assessments and fees for an address.

sections.h2: What is Amendment 3 and does it change a Cape Coral bill I owe?
sections.html:
Per the Lee County Tax Collector, Amendment 3 passed and takes effect January 1, 2027, so it does not alter a 2026 bill, which is due by March 31, 2027.

The city's own toolkit page describes the proposal's local effect: 91.4% of the city is residential and 60.8% of improved residential properties are homesteaded. The city estimates a $31.1 million revenue loss in year one and $56.9 million in year two, citing the Florida Office of Economic and Demographic Research. Those are the city's projections, not figures on your bill.

A sale does not bring the amendment into play before 2027. Ask the tax collector or your closing agent which tax year's bill your closing date triggers.

sections.h2: What are the Lee County tax dates a Cape Coral owner should know?
sections.html:
Value is fixed on New Year's Day, paperwork for exemptions closes at the start of March, and bills arrive in November with a final due date at the end of the following March.

Lee County calendar, from the appraiser and the tax collector
WhenWhat happens
January 1Date of assessment for all properties
March 1Filing deadline for all exemptions and agricultural classification
July 1Appraiser submits the assessment roll to the Department of Revenue
AugustTRIM notices mailed; 25 days from mailing to petition the Value Adjustment Board
NovemberBills mailed; 4% discount if paid in November
December, January, FebruaryDiscounts of 3%, 2% and 1%
March 31Bill due in full
April 1Unpaid taxes delinquent

The appraiser adds that an application filed after the deadline may still be granted, but for the following year.

sections.h2: Can I pay a Cape Coral property tax bill in installments?
sections.html:
Lee County has three ways to spread or postpone a bill: quarterly installments, partial payments and a homestead deferral.

Installment sign-up runs from the start of November through April 30, and a notice must show an estimate above $100. Four payments follow, with the first at a 6% discount, then 4.5%, then 3%, then nothing. The collector says the 2026 sign-up window closed April 30, 2026, so a new application would cover 2027 taxes.

  • Partial payments cover the current year only, allow up to five payments per account, earn no discount, cannot be made online and exclude delinquent taxes.
  • Homestead deferral: the tax collector sets March 31 as the application deadline, makes deferred tax a lien and requires fire insurance naming the office as loss payee.
  • A sale mid-plan leaves the buyer responsible for continuing that year's installments.

sections.h2: How do Cape Coral homeowners get homestead and appeal a value?
sections.html:
Applications go to the Lee County Property Appraiser. They are due March 1, and the house must be your permanent home on New Year's Day. Florida's exemption reaches $50,000 in two layers: $25,000 against every levy, then up to $25,000 more on value above $50,000 for non-school levies.

Save Our Homes then holds yearly growth in assessed value to 3 percent or inflation, whichever is smaller. Selling erases that built-up gap, so the next owner's bill can run well above yours. Portability lets part of the saving follow you to another Florida homestead, provided you set it up within the three-year window.

A value you dispute is challenged from the August TRIM notice. Lee County's appraiser allows 25 days after mailing for a Value Adjustment Board petition, and an informal conference with the appraiser is open all year.

sections.h2: How is the bill handled if I sell in Cape Coral?
sections.html:
At closing, the agent charges or credits each side its portion of the year, but the collector's FAQ says the bill for the whole year goes to the owner of record.

Forward a bill that reaches you after the sale to the buyer or the closing agent. The collector explains that ownership changes travel from the clerk to the appraiser, which can lag. Unpaid prior-year tax is delinquent after April 1 and gets paid off at closing like any other lien. Delinquent taxes cannot be paid by personal check or eCheck.

A deed carries Florida stamp tax of 70 cents on each $100 of consideration, and every signer shares liability for it. Look for the tax lines and prorations on your closing statement, and have the title company explain each one.

faqs.q: Which number reaches the Cape Coral appraiser?
faqs.a: Dial 239-533-6100 for value, exemption and address questions. Payments and receipts go through the collector's 239-533-6000 line.

faqs.q: Is Cape Coral's city millage rate 5.1471?
faqs.a: The city's news release says council approved the Fiscal Year 2027 budget on September 24 while maintaining the operating millage rate at 5.1471. Your total bill adds county, school and other authorities, so check your parcel on the tax collector's site.

faqs.q: When are Lee County taxes delinquent?
faqs.a: They go delinquent on April 1, the day after the March 31 deadline. Once delinquent, the tax collector will not take a personal check or eCheck.

faqs.q: Does the installment plan transfer when I sell?
faqs.a: The buyer picks it up. Lee County's collector says a new owner continues the plan for that tax year once installments have started, so settle who owes the remainder in the contract.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Cape Coral house with unpaid tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Any balance is cleared at closing from your proceeds, and the Lee County Tax Collector can tell you what is owed so the title company has the figure.
